hero.intro: Clothes are a lovely thing to give at Lunar New Year and an easy thing to get slightly wrong. A new piece carries a good meaning. Some colors and some objects carry meanings you never intended. Here is what to give, what to leave on the shelf, and how to pick a size you are guessing at.

sections.heading: What makes a good gift for chinese new year
paragraphs: Start with the custom that already points at clothes. Buying new clothing for the new year stands for a fresh start — you meet the year in something nobody has worn yet. One catch trips people up: buying new shoes for yourself belongs to that same custom, while giving shoes to somebody else is one of the classic things to avoid. Same object, opposite direction.

So the best gift for chinese new year is usually the piece she would have picked up for herself and did not. Something she can wear to the family lunch and again in March, in a color she already reaches for on an ordinary Tuesday.
bullets: Wearable on the day and after it: not a costume, not a keepsake
A color the family reads as festive rather than solemn
A size you can check against a piece she already owns
Nothing sitting on the avoid list two sections below

sections.heading: Gift for chinese new year 2026: the date and the horse
paragraphs: Lunar New Year 2026 falls on Tuesday, February 17, and it opens the Year of the Horse — a fire horse, in the sixty-year cycle that pairs each animal with an element, which is why you will see that phrase everywhere this time round. The public holiday in mainland China runs about a week, and the Spring Festival carries on to the Lantern Festival on the fifteenth day, so a slightly late gift still lands.

Set your own deadline well before February 17 rather than trusting a countdown clock on a website. We will not promise you a delivery date — carriers get busy around the holiday, and we would rather you had the piece in hand early than be refreshing a tracking page that morning. Our pieces arrive in small runs too, so the one you liked may be gone by the weekend.

sections.heading: The traditional gift for chinese new year, and the ones to skip
paragraphs: The traditional gift for chinese new year is money in a red envelope. Married adults pass them to the younger members of the family, and the digits matter more than the total: amounts ending in eight are the favored ones, because eight sounds like the word for prosperity, while anything built on four is left alone, because four sounds like the word for death. Offer the envelope with both hands, and take one back the same way.
The list of things not to give is longer than most people expect, and plenty of families keep it. Nearly all of it is one word sounding like another.

That last line matters most when the gift is clothing. If the family keeps the custom closely, leave the white piece and the black one on the rail and reach for something warm: pink, rose, plum, soft gold, a deep brown. A color nobody has to interpret is the gentler choice when you are giving.
bullets: Clocks and watches — giving a clock sounds like seeing someone off at the end of a life
Knives, scissors, anything sharp — they read as cutting the relationship
Umbrellas — the word sounds like splitting up
Shoes — it sounds like the word for evil
Mirrors and wallets — a breakable thing, and sending your fortune away
Anything grouped in fours, and anything white or black, the colors of a funeral

sections.heading: A gift for chinese mom, and gifts for asian moms who own everything
paragraphs: A gift for chinese mom is almost never about a shortage of things. It is about the piece she kept putting back because she was busy buying for everybody else. A knit with real weight in the hand, a wrap dress for lunch out, a skirt with a detail that gets her asked where it came from. One piece, wrapped properly, beats a pile.

Two words of care with gifts for asian moms. Asia is many countries and many households, and a mother in Seoul, one in Bangkok and one in Houston do not share a taste because a search box filed them together. Notice what she actually wore the last three times you saw her, then shop for that. Our Asia edit holds the Korean and Thai pieces; the affordable luxury rail holds the ones that feel like a gift coming out of the tissue paper.

If you are hunting a gift for asian mom and you honestly do not know her measurements, pick something that forgives: a wrap front, a tie waist, a soft knit. Then read the numbers, because a maker in Korea and a maker in Thailand rarely agree on what medium means. Our size guide shows you how to compare, and the return policy covers a gift that has to come back.

sections.heading: A gift for asian dad, honestly
paragraphs: Here is the answer we owe you. We are a womenswear boutique, so we cannot dress him, and we are not going to point you at a unisex page and hope you do not notice. What we can hand over is the etiquette, and that travels: keep him off the avoid list — no clock, no knife set, no shoes — and think about what he already does rather than what a gift guide says a father should like.
One thing worth saying out loud: at many tables the gift for the household is the one that gets remembered. If his wife opens something she loves at the same lunch, you did well by both.

sections.heading: Gift for chinese wedding: the envelope comes first
paragraphs: At a Chinese wedding the expected gift from a guest is cash in a red envelope rather than a boxed thing off a registry. The digit rules hold: crisp notes, even numbers, amounts ending in eight where you can manage it, nothing with a four in it, both hands. How much depends on how close you are to the couple and where the wedding is, so ask another guest rather than a stranger on the internet.

Which moves the shopping to what you wear. Guests are usually steered away from white and black, the colors tied to mourning, and red is often left to the couple — worth checking with whoever invited you, because families differ. That leaves a wide and lovely middle: blush, plum, sage, dusty rose, soft gold, warm brown. Our wedding guest rail is picked for that middle, and the petite dresses run is there if hems normally need a seamstress.

sections.heading: Gifts for chinese gift exchange: set the bracket first
paragraphs: Two things share a name here. The office game where everyone brings one wrapped item and steals from each other is often called a Chinese gift exchange, or a white elephant, and it has nothing to do with Lunar New Year customs. If that is the one on your calendar, agree the price cap before anybody buys, then shop to it.

The best gifts for chinese gift exchange still work on whoever ends up holding them, which rules out guessing a size in front of a room. We are a clothing boutique, so most of what we carry has a size on the label — if the exchange is blind, choose a piece with no fitting to it, or buy where returns are straightforward. Ours sit in the return policy.

faqs.q: When is Chinese New Year in 2026?
faqs.a: Tuesday, February 17, 2026. It opens the Year of the Horse, and in the sixty-year cycle that pairs animals with elements this one is a fire horse. The public holiday in mainland China runs about a week, and the wider Spring Festival continues to the Lantern Festival on the fifteenth day. If you are posting a gift for chinese new year 2026, work backward from February 17 and leave yourself room.

faqs.q: Is clothing a good gift for chinese new year?
faqs.a: Yes, and the custom backs it up: new clothing for the new year stands for a fresh start. Two rules keep it safe. Leave white and black pieces out of it, since those are the colors tied to funerals, and do not give shoes, because the word sounds like the word for evil — even though buying your own new shoes is part of the tradition.

faqs.q: What should I never give at Lunar New Year?
faqs.a: Clocks and watches, knives and scissors, umbrellas, pears, shoes, mirrors, wallets, anything grouped in fours, and anything in white or black. Most of it comes from words that sound alike: giving a clock sounds like seeing someone off at the end of a life, umbrella sounds like splitting up, pear sounds like parting. Families keep these to different degrees, and nobody has ever been upset by a gift that quietly sidestepped all of them.

faqs.q: How much money goes in the envelope for a gift for chinese wedding?
faqs.a: There is no single figure and we will not make one up. What stays consistent is the shape of it: cash in a red envelope, crisp notes, even numbers, amounts ending in eight where you can, nothing containing a four, handed over with both hands. Closeness to the couple sets the size of it, and what counts as usual varies by family and by city, so ask another guest.

faqs.q: Do you sell menswear for a gift for asian dad?
faqs.a: No. We are a womenswear boutique and we would rather say so plainly than sell you something with a shrug. The etiquette above still helps: nothing sharp, no clock, no shoes, and think about what he already uses rather than what a list says he should want. If you are buying for a whole household, the piece his wife opens is often the one everyone talks about.

faqs.q: How do I pick a size when the gift is a surprise?
faqs.a: Read the measurement table on the product page rather than the size letter, because makers across Asia grade differently and one label's medium is another's large. Then measure a piece she already wears, laid flat, and compare the numbers. A wrap front, a tie waist or a soft knit forgives a near miss. If it still lands wrong, the return policy on the site sets out how it can come back.
